your_life.name: Inspector Arun Mehra
your_life.recollections:
Before the district office, before the uniform, there was Mill Lane: the rasp of your father's wheel plane through the open workshop door and Tara making you wait while she tied her shoes. You left Bhairav's Hollow with a habit of looking back at the chapel turn. Twelve winters have passed since Mercy House sent the letter saying your sister had died of fever. Requests for the original papers have filled a drawer in your room at headquarters; the paper has aged more visibly than the answers have changed.

Leena used to know where you kept that drawer. You lived together for three years, separated, and learned to write letters about the practical things that remained. Her mother once set tea in front of you after Tara's funeral. Raghav's signature is familiar from replies to your requests. You remember the weight of the cup and the silence around it.

Kabir has worked beside you for six years. You remember the floodwater in the cellar where you pulled him out, but also uneventful journeys, poor meals and the little habits by which colleagues become familiar. Dr. Mira Sen's invitation brought you back on leave: she wanted to discuss an old family record. No death had been reported when you set out. Now the coach journey is behind you, the town is under snow, and you have reached Mercy House.

now.immediately_visible: A woman lies motionless beside the archive desk.

place.name: Mercy House archive
place.description: The lamps have been turned up too high. Above their yellow circles the archive disappears into beams and soot, and each time the wind presses against the casement the flames lean together. A desk stands under the window, its blotter crowded by ordinary papers. Beyond it are shelves, a cold fireplace and a service door whose lower edge has worn a pale arc into the boards. From the scullery comes the intermittent complaint of a kettle. The narrow opening catches a line of light from the adjoining kitchen.

findings.label: folded sheet
findings.description: A thin sheet has been folded along the same lines until the paper has worn almost white. In Tara’s hand: “Please keep what I actually said. The director ordered the door locked. I asked Matron Das to let me out. She refused. If another copy is made, do not let that sentence disappear.” The remaining lines concern cold bedding and a request for clean clothes.

findings.label: folded note
findings.description: “Keep out of the burial office. Before the ninth bell I shall silence you. — Dev”

findings.label: body
findings.description: The woman has no detectable pulse. There is a recent injury at the temple and wet blood beneath her head.

findings.label: brass seal
findings.description: A heavy seal lies beside the desk. Dark wet staining marks one edge.

findings.label: torn cuff
findings.description: A small scrap of dark wool is caught under the desk edge. It is not a complete garment.

place.name: Mercy House entrance hall
place.description: Meltwater drops steadily from the coats along the wall. The entrance hall smells of damp wool, lamp oil and the polish used on the visitors' book stand. One passage leads back to the archive, another to the scullery; the courtyard door knocks softly against its latch. Farther along, the ninth ward remains bolted. There is room for two people to pass comfortably here, provided neither chooses to stand in the way.

findings.label: visitors book
findings.description: Names and arrival times. Several pages have been folded at the corner.

findings.label: folded envelope
findings.description: The envelope has no stamp. Inside, a hurried letter begins: “Kabir—Savitri paid me to carry two sealed grave crates to Dev’s winter beds. I took the cart after the last bell, as she asked. I was told not to stop at the house. The stable kept a duplicate of the charge. Please keep me out of this; I cannot have your uniform at my door. Nalin.” A second fold has tucked the signature out of sight.

place.name: Mercy House scullery
place.description: The scullery is warmer than the rest of the house, but the warmth ends at the floor. A range holds a kettle and a blackened pan; a wash basin waits beneath the window. Beside the range, the service hatch opens onto a sliver of the archive desk. Standing at it, you can see how a person might notice a sleeve or a moving hand and miss the face above it. Doors return to the archive and entrance hall.

place.name: Mercy House courtyard
place.description: Snow collects along the courtyard walls without yet settling in the wheel ruts. A gate lamp turns the falling flakes into brief bright scratches. Behind you Mercy House has too many dark windows; ahead, the road drops toward the square. A narrower way runs beside the wall to Dev's winter garden. A kitchen clang carries into the courtyard and is gone almost before you turn toward it.

place.name: Dev’s house and winter garden
place.description: Dev's house shelters behind winter beds edged with salvaged slate. Snow has softened most of the garden into one surface, broken by the tool shed and the kitchen table visible under a lean-to. Somewhere under the beds are last month's bulbs; from where you stand you cannot tell whether anything more recent lies beneath them. A path follows the fence toward the cemetery, while the courtyard lamp remains visible behind you.

findings.label: disturbed soil
findings.description: The soil above last month’s bulbs has recently been lifted. The depression is longer than a garden trench.

place.name: Town square
place.description: The square has emptied before the shops have quite closed. Shutters answer one another across the road, and a horse drinks noisily at the trough beneath the notice board. The Pine Lantern keeps a strip of light under its door. Paths lead toward the chapel, the Das and Rao households, and the Mercy House courtyard; beyond the last lamp the forest road becomes a different shade of black. You remember this crossing from childhood, though the signs above the shops have changed.

place.name: Pine Lantern inn
place.description: The Pine Lantern's dining room has divided itself into people waiting for news and people pretending to finish supper. A lodging book rests behind the counter. Wet boots have made dark half-moons around the stove. The road outside leads back into the square, where the coach will stop at dawn if the snow allows it.

place.name: Das household

Beside the stove stands an ash bucket; across the room, a writing desk has been closed and locked. Everything has the cared-for appearance of objects kept through more winters than their owners expected. The only street door returns to the square.

args.narrative: The threatening folded note recovered from the archive desk reads “Keep out of the burial office. Before the ninth bell I shall silence you. — Dev” (r2). Its signature alone does not establish the writer or origin. I did not acquire comparative writing samples or physical/documentary evidence establishing that the note was fabricated, so I make no attribution or fabrication finding. A separate folded envelope found in the hall (r9) contains a letter attributed within its text to Nalin, describing Savitri's payment for carrying sealed grave crates; it does not connect anyone to the threatening note. Witness answers (r6, r7, r10, r12) supply no direct identification of the note's writer or source. The statement about Tara in r1 is separate and not a basis for attributing the threat.

result.limitations: Structured propositions and authored alternative proof paths are scored. Narrative is unscored; this is not a general natural-language fact checker.
